findings.title: Recreate exit code changed from 4 to 3, and 4 now means 'feature disabled'
findings.body: `RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE` changes from 4 to 3, and exit code 4 is reassigned to `FEATURE_DISABLED`. Scripts written against the previous behavior treat exit code 4 as 'recreate needed'. After this change they will misread the result: a real recreate requirement (now 3) may be treated as an unexpected error, and a disabled feature (now 4) may be read as 'recreate needed'. This is a silent change to a documented, scriptable contract. It needs at least a release or migration note.

findings.title: New exit codes are not asserted
findings.body: `testFeatureNotEnabled` only checks the error message. It never asserts that the exit code is 4 (`FEATURE_DISABLED`). It also covers only the `metadata` subcommand, not `check`. `testWrongVersions` never asserts the new recreate exit code of 3. A regression in the exit-code contract, which is what scripts depend on, would therefore go unnoticed.
